name: Prickly Pear

facts.what: Red fruit (tunas); young pads (nopales) in spring
facts.how: Fruit raw, juiced, or as jelly; pads grilled or boiled
facts.when: Tunas July to September, pads in spring
facts.where: Dry ground statewide, thickest in the west

caution: The hair-fine glochids are worse than the big spines. Tongs, thick gloves, and a flame to singe them off are not optional.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Twist tunas off with tongs into a bucket and never touch them bare-handed until they are singed or peeled. For nopales, take bright young pads in spring and slice off every eye.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Tunas peel into a magenta fruit that juices beautifully; strain the seeds. Nopales grill like a vegetable and pair naturally with eggs, onion, and chile.
